Commentary.Commentary: That concludes the proceedings for the second T20I. The last match of this series is on Thursday, 1st April 2021, in Auckland at 1900 local (0600 GMT). You can join us well in advance for the build-up. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Tim Southee, the captain of New Zealand, starts by calling it an unusual game with the rain around but he is glad that his boys adjusted well. Tells that it's been a great summer and they were privileged to have teams travel here in these times. Southee admits that Bangladesh did put them under pressure. Praises Glenn Phillips for doing a great job with the wet ball and shares that he just went with his gut feeling regarding the bowling changes. Informs that the slower deliveries were holding up. He is pleased to get over the line and is now looking to end their summer on a high.

Mahmudullah, the captain of Bangladesh, starts by saying there was a bit of confusion related to the DLS target. Feels they were on track in the first 10 overs but then lost the plot in the next 6. States that Naim and Sarkar gave them the momentum but Sodhi and Phillips' overs were extremely good and they failed to capitalize. Shares that Taskin's outstanding catch gave them a lot of confidence. Feels that it's important to finish well in the T20 format which is not happening for them at the moment. Mentions that the top order has been in great form and hopes to take the positives into the next match.

Glenn Phillips is chosen for the Man of the Match award! Says that they were trying to hit the ball hard and run a lot of twos. Talking about Daryl Mitchell, Phillips mentions that to have a partner at the other end who is on fire really helps. Tells that there is always a dilemma regarding DLS when you're thinking about going hard or saving wickets as it might affect the equation. States that he has been working on his bowling and it's always about handling nerves.

Earlier in the match, we witnessed a good bowling and fielding show from Bangladesh, for a change. However, the rain break spoiled their good work as New Zealand managed to bounce back through the powerful stand between Glenn Phillips and Daryl Mitchell. Their scintillating hitting provided the late surge to the Kiwis and due to that the revised target for Bangladesh, turned out to be more than enough in the end.

The chase of Bangladesh was all about the partnership between Mohammad Naim and Soumya Sarkar. They batted with authority and managed to steal the momentum away from New Zealand. The pair started the onslaught by targeting Ish Sodhi's first over which went for 19 runs and followed that up with 20 runs from Adam Milne's second over. However, Tim Southee's decision to hand the ball to Glenn Phillips, the part-timer, did the magic for the Blackcaps. He bowled a very tidy first over and then Sodhi redeemed himself by delivering a 5-run over after that. Due to a couple of dry overs, the required rate mounted and it resulted in the wickets of first Sarkar and then Naim. The chase derailed after that with the Kiwi bowlers finding the target and bowling enough good balls to defend the total.

End of a rain-truncated game and New Zealand have taken an unassailable lead in the 3-match T20I series. Once again Bangladesh chose to offer a fight in the second match of the series but again it was not enough to beat New Zealand. The Blackcaps have now extended their dominance this summer after bagging their 7th series at home.
NEW ZEALAND WIN BY 28 RUNS (DLS METHOD)! Too full in length on middle, almost served in the blockhole, Mahedi drives it down the ground for a run.

Comedy again! Fuller length ball around leg, a knuckle delivery, Hasan heaves it over mid-wicket. Two fielders converge, Phillips and Allen. Both leave it for each other before Glenn realizes and picks the ball. Two taken.
Another wide down the leg side! It's been left alone by Mahedi.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, left alone.

OUT! Taken this time, by Southee! Bennett finally gets his wicket. Slower one, on a length around off, Saifuddin swings his bat blindly and gets a big top edge. Southee settles underneath it at extra cover.

What happened there? Miscommunication between Southee and Guptill. A knuckle delivery, around off, Mahedi mistimes it in the air over extra cover and Southee from inside the ring and Guptill from long off go for it. The former leaves it alone thinking that the latter will go for it, Guptill does the same. Funny! The ball drops right in the middle of them. One run taken.
SIX! Short in length and close to off, Mahedi gets across and is through with his shot early. Still packs it with good power and the ball clears the fence at square leg.
Shortish and on middle, pulled towards mid-wicket for a run.
Hamish Bennett to bowl the final over of the match.
A dipping yorker on off, Saifuddin digs it out to the off side for a single.
DRS time! Shout for an lbw! Not given. Southee has decided to review it.

NOT OUT! Missing leg. A length ball around middle and leg, angling down, Mahedi tries to heave it across the line but misses. He is pinged on the front pad, they appeal but the umpire disagrees. Tim takes the DRS as the batsmen cross. The Ball Tracker finds it to be missing the leg pole.
Miscued! Pitches it up and wide outside off, Saifuddin reaches out to play the lofted shot over covers. But it takes the toe end and flies towards mid off. Drops safely, a single is taken.
Another swing and a miss! Slower one, on a length outside off at 106 kph, Saifuddin is early into his shot and misses.
Short in length on middle, Saifuddin advances down the track and tries to swing it over the leg side, misses.
Mohammad Saifuddin is the new batsman in.

OUT! Caught behind! Just helped into Conway's gloves. The wheels are coming off rather quickly for Bangladesh. A knuckle-ball around middle and leg, Mithun tries to play the paddle scoop but doesn't have any pace to work with. Ends up inside edging it towards the keeper who dives across to his left to complete a fantastic catch.
Full in length and outside off, steered through backward point for two runs.
Mahedi Hasan is the new batsman in.

OUT! Sound of timber! Pace does the trick for Adam Milne this time. Good length ball around off, at 141 kph, Afif swings his bat at it but fails to connect and the off stump is pegged back. Milne has bounced back here well!
Width on offer outside off, Mithun edges it down to third man for a run.
Mohammad Mithun is the next batsman in.

OUT! CLATTERED! The slower one does the trick for the speed merchant. Milne bowls it on a length and in the line of the stumps at 116 kph, Mahmudullah shuffles across the stumps for the paddle scoop but it arrives late to beat his bat and finds the stumps. New Zealand inching closer to sealing the deal.
FOUR! Streaky boundary, not Milne's night. Spears in a full ball on middle and leg, Mahmudullah tries to flick but it takes the inner half, beats the stumps and races away to the fine leg fence.
Too full in length and on middle, Hossain whips it through mid-wicket for a run.
Adam Milne is back on.
FOUR! This one probably slips out of Phillips' hand. A full toss outside off, Mahmudullah attacks it and lofts it over backward point for a boundary. 8 runs and a wicket from the over.
Follows the batsman down the leg side with a shortish ball, Afif tries his best to cut but misses. Conway also fails to connect and they take a bye.
Short and on off, Mahmudullah goes back and cuts it through cover-point for a run.
Aerial but safe! Flatter and around off, Afif tries to heave but gets it away off the top edge. It beats the despairing dive of the extra cover fielder and they take a run.
Flighted and outside off, driven through covers for a single.
Afif Hossain is the new batsman in.

OUT! Phillips strikes to get his first international wicket! Naim is also out of here and the asking rate gets the better of him. The pressure was mounting on him. Full and floated on off, Naim aims to clear long off but gets more height than distance. Guptill comes running in from the deep and takes the simplest of catches. 60 needed off 23 balls and this match is drifting away from Bangladesh now.
Glenn Phillips is back on. 2-0-13-0 are his figures so far.
Forces a full ball back past the bowler and by the time the long off fielder gets around, they take a couple of runs. 10 from the over!
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries! Tossed up ball around off, Mahmudullah brings out the reverse sweep and lets it fly over short third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Good spot to hit the ball! Full and around off, Mahmudullah throws his bat at it and smashes it behind the bowler for a boundary. A much-needed one for Bangladesh.
Too wide outside off, hitting the blockhole, Mahmudullah mistimes his drive through the line. Three dots.
Another play and a miss! Full and flighted outside off, Mahmudullah tries to smash it over covers but it spins past his bat.
Play and a miss! Quicker and flatter outside off, Mahmudullah attempts to cut but misses.
Ish Sodhi is back on. 24 in his 2 overs so far.
Another knuckle delivery, short and wide outside off at 109.5 kph, Naim is deceived and misses. 70 needed off 30 balls, the match is now slipping away from Bangladesh.
Slower one, on a length and around leg, Naim stays leg side and tries to work around but ends up pushing it back to Tim.
Top edge, safe! Short in length around leg, Naim top edges his pull shot and it flies behind. Bennett tries his best to reach it from short fine leg but it drops safely. They take two.
Back of a length ball on off, Mahmudullah hangs back and drags it down to wide long on for one.

Errors after errors! Fuller in length around off, Naim drives it towards extra cover and speeds to the other end. Sodhi has a needless shy at the bowler's end but misses. The fielder in the deep tries to back-up but fumbles and the batsmen get two overthrows, three runs in total added to the scoreboard. Southee is not pleased.
Mahmudullah is the new batsman in.

OUT! Southee removes the dangerous batsman! A clever delivery, short and outside off, off-pace, Sarkar hops back to make room and then has to reach out for the ball. Ends up mistiming it towards long on where Milne takes a fine catch. End of an outstanding knock and a threatening stand which was worth 81 off 52 balls. 76 needed off 35 balls.
Tim Southee is back for his third over.
On middle, Naim looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Full on off, Naim lofts it over covers. The batsmen get two runs.

Loopy delivery on off, Naim pushes it back towards the bowler where Phillips does well to stop it. Sarkar was backing up too far. Phillips does not throw it on the stumps at his end otherwise it would have been close.
Floated delivery on off, Sarkar drives it through mid off for a single.
FOUR! 50 for Soumya Sarkar, off just 25 balls! It has been a lovely innings from him. Short again on middle, Sarkar pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short ball on middle, Sarkar pulls it through mid-wicket. Two runs taken.
Loopy and around leg, Sarkar works it to mid-wicket for a run. A good comeback over by Sodhi. Two excellent overs by the Kiwis on the trot, taking the RRR to 12.14.
Quicker one, around leg, Sarkar mishits it back to the bowler.
Attempts a reverse-batted shot and drags it off the inner half to short third man for a run.

DROPPED? Yes, Glenn Phillips gets there and nearly pulled off the catch of the year. That was some effort, we won't call it a dropped catch, a normal fielder would not have even reached it. If not the catch of the year, this certainly is the dive of the year. Wow. Airborne. Beautiful capture. Flighted and full around leg, Naim tries to heave it over square leg but top edges it towards deep mid-wicket. Two fielders converge and it's Phillips who attempts with a superb dive forward but fails to hang on. Two taken.
Follows the batsman down the leg side with a fuller ball, Sarkar drives it through extra cover for one.
Flighted and full outside off, Sarkar tries to reverse sweep but misses.
Ish Sodhi is back on. 1-0-19-0 are his figures so far.
Top edge/back edge! Tossed up ball landing full on middle, Sarkar tries to reverse sweep but miscues it behind the keeper. A single to end a tidy over.
Short and wide outside off, cut through point for a single. Just 3 from the over, can Glenn finish it off well?
Flatter and shorter on middle, punched down to long on for a single.
Another appeal for an lbw! Once again there is an inside edge. Flatter and fuller on off, Sarkar tries to slog sweep but gets an inside edge onto the back leg.
Shout for an lbw! Nothing from the umpire. A slider around off, skidding in, Sarkar stays back to play it late but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Short and wide outside off, cut through cover-point for a run.
Glenn Phillips is into the attack.
Shortish and on off, angling away, Naim taps it down to the off side and they cross for a brisk single. 20 from this over, 39 in the last two, 94 needed off 54 balls.
Wide! The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Misses! Short in length and on middle, skidding off the surface, Naim hangs back to play the upper cut but misses.

FOUR! Bangladesh are flying at the moment, it's a buffet of big hitting at the moment. Fuller in length on middle, Naim clears his front leg and hammers it over the head of the mid on fielder for a boundary.
Fullish and angling down the leg side, Sarkar clips it down to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Good length ball around off, Sarkar rocks back and slaps it through cover-point for a run.

SIX! What a shot! Sarkar is 39 off 14 and he is certainly motoring along. Short in length around off, Soumya gives himself room and muscles it over third man for a biggie. Milne has overstepped as well. Free Hit loading.

FOUR! That's thumped! Clean striking on display here. Fuller in length around middle, from 'round the wicket, Sarkar picks it up and whips it past the mid-wicket fielder inside the ring for a boundary. Bangladesh are ahead of the DLS par score at the moment.
Adam Milne is back into the attack. He bowled a fiery first over and conceded just 6 runs.
Misses out! Flatter and shorter delivery outside off, Naim tries to cut but fails. 19 from Ish's first over. 114 needed off 60 balls.
Flatter and shorter on off, Sarkar goes back and punches it down to long on for a run.
SIX! Soumya is putting Ish Sodhi to the sword. Almost a replay of the last shot. Flighted and full on middle, Sarkar smokes it all the way over mid-wicket. Pressure on the leggie.
SIX! High and handsome! A tossed up ball landing full on middle, Sarkar brings out the conventional slog sweep this time and nails it into the stands at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Innovative from Sarkar. Classy. Loopy delivery, full and around off, Sarkar gets into the position early for the reverse-batted shot and powers it over backward point for a boundary.
Short again, skidding away from the batsman from around off, Naim punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Wide! A googly, short and way wide outside off, Naim tries to cut but misses.
Here comes the champion bowler - Ish Sodhi. He just took 11 balls to derail Bangladesh's chase in the last game. What's in store today?
Back of a length delivery outside off, Soumya cuts it through point for a single. 7 from the over, Powerplay is done and dusted now!
Slower one, on a good length around middle and off, Sarkar sticks back and plays it down wide of backward point for a run.

FOUR! Cracking shot! Short in length and around off, Sarkar hops back to make room and smashes it over the cover fielder for a boundary. Just a little bit of momentum has started to come into Bangladesh's innings now.
Fullish and on off, Naim drives it down to mid off and scampers across to the other end.
A cutter this time, it's hurled across the left-hander, Naim tries to cut but misses.
Swing and a miss! Short and outside off, zipping away from the batsman, Naim swishes and misses.
Change in bowling. Tim Southee is back on. One more over before we will have an official game.

Short in length again, outside off, this time Sarkar leans back and cuts it aerially through point. Phillips makes a sliding stop in the deep and the batsmen take two. 11 from the over, 140 needed more off 72 balls.
Short in length and outside off, Naim cuts it in the air but safely over point. There is a fielder in the deep, so only a run is available.
Good length ball on off, angling away, Naim punches but finds the extra cover fielder.

FOUR! Crashed! Back of a length ball on middle and off, Naim rocks back, rides the bounce and plunders it over mid-wicket. One bounce and into the fence it goes. The young man is delighting everyone with his shots!
FOUR! Good shot! Short in length and outside off, angling away, this time Naim stays put, watches the ball closely and just times his square cut through the gap at backward point.
Swing and a miss! Fuller in length and outside off, Naim throws his bat at it but fails to connect. Trying too hard!

Chance of a run out, missed! Shortish and outside off, Naim cuts it towards cover-point where the fielder makes a half-stop. The point fielder picks up the ball, has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Sarkar was not even in the frame. Lucky escape, top over by Adam!

Miscued shot! Milne is making a statement with his extra pace. Short and on off, hurrying the batsman, Sarkar tries to pull but it takes the toe end and runs wide of the diving point fielder for a run.
That's another one, right through! Milne is bowling with a lot of fire. 147 kph delivery, on a shortish length outside off, Sarkar flashes and misses. Conway collects it well.
Pace and movement, Sarkar is beaten again. A length ball on middle and off, nipping away, Sarkar goes nowhere with his feet, tries pushing inside the line and misses.
Beaten! Excessive pace from Milne. Too full and outside off, Sarkar tries to hit down but misses.
FOUR! Driven beautifully! Milne starts with an overpitched delivery outside off, Sarkar gets forward and strokes it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
Soumya Sarkar is the new batsman. Adam Milne is also into the attack now.

OUT! Liton holes out! Well caught in the deep by Glenn Phillips. Short in length and on middle, Das goes for the pull shot but it comes from the higher half of his bat and travels to the fielder in the deep at mid-wicket. Phillips grabs a nice low catch and Bangladesh lose their first wicket. The shot was on but the extra bounce probably proved to be Liton's downfall. 157 needed off 84 balls.
Goes aerial, Naim. Lofts a length ball over cover-point. There is a protection in the deep and hence, only a run taken.
A touch short and on off, Naim stays back to play it down to point. Dot again.
CONFIRMED NOW! DLS is very tough to understand, have to say. 171 is the magic number, in 16 overs. We already have 9 balls bowled, so please do the maths. Bennett to resume his spell...

Hang on a minute! The two umpires get together and have stopped the play. Jeff Crowe, the match referee, is working on the sheet for the revised target. It was 148 in 16 overs initially. Let's see if there is any change. Haven't seen this before. A bit bizarre!
Mishit! Short in length and on middle, Naim hangs back to pull but mistimes it towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! That's a great boundary! Back of a length delivery outside off, angling away, Naim hangs on the back foot and punches it sweetly through point for a boundary. For your information, we are yet to hear from the match referee for the official revised target. We shall let you know if there is any change!
A yorker length ball on off, dipping in, Liton keeps his eyes on the delivery and digs it out towards mid off for a run.
Wide! A loosener, on a good length and angling down the leg side, Das fails to get any bat on it.
Hamish Bennett to speed in from the other end.
Fuller and on middle, Naim gets behind the line and pushes it back to the bowler. 6 from the first over!
Short in length and around leg, Naim is hurried into his pull shot and he ends up playing it to mid-wicket.
A length ball on off, Liton pushes it towards mid off and scampers to the other end.

FOUR! That's one way to tackle movement. Liton advances down the track to a good length delivery and flat-bats it over the bowler's end. Not quite gets hold of the shot but still has made enough connection to send it past the fence.
Beaten! An extra bit of zip from the surface. On a good length and close to off, seaming away, Das feels for it inside the line and misses.
Starts with a length ball around off, a little bit of away movement, Naim pushes it to covers and gets off the mark with a single.
